title: Integrated Standard10 greedy-boundary missing-objective audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The seven-objective reward-plus-forward-KL direction and its selected 5e-5 updates systematically worsen the Standard10 greedy-margin boundary in both independent 1M lineages, explaining mixed fresh greedy breadth; adding the release-aware greedy boundary as an eighth normalized objective yields a strict common descent direction.
material_change: No new hands or updates. Reconstruct the immutable 12,288-hand cohort, compute the existing release-aware Standard10 greedy-margin loss/gradient with max margin 0.1 and release advantage 1.0, audit parent/control/treatment boundary changes, and solve the eight-objective minimum-norm geometry in both lineages.
notes: Preregistered admission requires nonzero boundary gradients, negative seven-direction/boundary cosine, observed seven-treatment boundary loss increase, and a valid positive-worst-alignment eight-objective solution in both lineages. Failure of any replication gate rejects this specific missing-objective explanation.
No policy updates, new hands, or Slumbot calls. The specific boundary-aware route is closed by replicated mechanism evidence, not by early external score.

result.summary: The release-aware Standard10 greedy-boundary gradient was nonzero and an eight-objective common descent direction existed, but the preregistered missing-objective mechanism failed: the existing seven-objective direction aligned positively with the boundary in both lineages (+0.094/+0.077), and source KL aligned very strongly (+0.863/+0.947). The finite 5e-5 treatment nevertheless increased boundary loss in both.
result.conclusion: Greedy-boundary degradation at the selected dose is another nonlinear finite-step crossing, not evidence that forward KL points in the wrong direction or that an eighth boundary objective is missing. Do not add a boundary-specific loss based on this result. The Standard10 greedy-vs-sampled clue remains relevant to evaluation contracts, but it does not justify this intervention.
result.next_step: Return to the long-horizon learned-policy objective. Implement a minimal on-policy conflict diagnostic that preserves opponent identity in transitions and measures per-minibatch common-descent feasibility across fixed anchors, dynamic snapshots, self-play, and source KL before changing the optimizer. Use a short contract smoke to establish metadata/replay correctness; do not scale or call Slumbot until online geometry is known.
